question: Do people read about the same parts of Seoul that foreign visitors actually walk into?

answer: We cannot say. We set out to put reading next to walking and found the public table can only be asked about 5 of 24 districts — too few to answer, and Gangnam is not among them. What the gap shows is where the counting stops, not where people go.
cannotSay: These two rulers count different people. The reading is from four Southeast Asian Wikipedias; the admissions count every foreign visitor, from anywhere.
They also cover different time. The reading is the twelve months to July 2026; the admissions are the calendar year 2023.

These are paid tourist sites only. A district whose draw is a street, a market or a shopping area — Gangnam among them — records few admissions here, and that is the ruler talking, not the visitors. It also counts admissions, not people: one visitor entering three sites is three.

The source records a foreign-visitor count of 0 for districts that plainly receive foreign visitors — Songpa, which holds Lotte World, is one of them with 7.7m admissions and 0 foreigners. We do not correct the source. We mark those rows and leave them out of any share we publish.
readingIsNotVisiting: A read is curiosity, not a trip. It cannot say who came, only who looked. Arrival counts by nationality are published separately by the Korea Tourism Organization and are the right instrument for visits.
finding: Korea's public admissions table can speak for 5 of Seoul's 24 districts. In 16 of them it counts no tourist site at all — among them Jung (Myeongdong) and Mapo (Hongdae). In 3 more it counts admissions but records foreign visitors as zero: Gangnam, Songpa, Gangseo.
bothRulersAreIncomplete: Seoul has 25 districts. The Southeast Asian Wikipedias hold an article for 24 of them — Yangcheon has none in any of the four. The admissions table can be asked about 5. Neither ruler sees the whole city.
